title: Cracking long hydrocarbons into useful ones

explain.say: Here is a puzzle. Crude oil gives lots of long, gloopy molecules like fuel oil, but people want far more petrol. What can you do with the leftovers? Look at the board. You start with a long alkane, decane, with 10 carbon atoms.

explain.say: See the flame? You heat the long hydrocarbon until it is a hot vapour. Heat makes the molecules shake very hard. What do you think might happen to a long chain shaking that hard?

stages.label: Long alkane
stages.note: e.g. decane, C10H22, from fuel oil.

stages.label: Over a catalyst
stages.ask: Why is a catalyst used in cracking?

explain.say: It can snap! Look at the scissors. The hot vapour passes over a catalyst, which helps the bonds break, and the long chain cracks into shorter pieces. That is why it is called cracking. Can you guess what the shorter pieces are used for?

explain.say: Look at the last step. Decane cracks into octane, for petrol, and ethene, a small molecule with a double bond, called an alkene. Count the carbons: 8 plus 2 makes 10, so nothing is lost. Why do you think factories want ethene?

stages.label: Long alkane
stages.note: e.g. decane, C10H22, from fuel oil.

stages.label: Over a catalyst
stages.ask: Why is a catalyst used in cracking?

explain.say: To make plastics! Great work. Look at the board: crude oil has more long chains than we need and too few short ones, and cracking fixes that. Wow: ethene from cracking becomes polythene, the plastic in bags and bottles you see all over the world.

faq.a: Cracking breaks long hydrocarbon molecules into shorter, more useful ones by heating them, usually with a catalyst. It makes petrol and alkenes like ethene.

faq.q: Why is a catalyst used in cracking?
faq.a: The catalyst lowers the energy needed to break the bonds, so cracking happens faster and at a lower temperature, saving energy.
asks: What does the catalyst do in cracking?

faq.a: Ethene is used to make poly(ethene), or polythene, and other chemicals like ethanol. Plants also make it as a gas that ripens fruit.
Crude oil contains more long-chain fractions than people need and not enough short ones, like petrol. Cracking turns the surplus long chains into the short ones in demand.

faq.q: How do you balance a cracking equation?
faq.a: The carbons and hydrogens must add up on both sides. Decane, C10H22, gives octane, C8H18, plus ethene, C2H4: 8 plus 2 carbons, and 18 plus 4 hydrogens.

facts: Cracking of decane: C10H22 → C8H18 + C2H4.
Cracking produces alkanes and alkenes; alkenes such as ethene are used to make polymers.

quiz.say: Complete the cracking equation: C12H26 → C8H18 + ?
quiz.show: Complete the cracking equation: C12H26 → C8H18 + ?
quiz.why: 12 minus 8 is 4 carbons, and 26 minus 18 is 8 hydrogens, so C4H8.

wrong.0: That gives 28 hydrogens in total, two too many.
wrong.1: That leaves one carbon atom out.

quiz.say: Why do refineries crack long hydrocarbons?
quiz.show: Why do refineries crack long hydrocarbons?

options.show: To make more of the short chains people need
options.say: To make more of the short chains people need

quiz.why: Demand for short chains like petrol is higher than crude oil supplies.

wrong.0: The products are still hydrocarbons containing carbon.
wrong.2: Cracking breaks chains; it does not join them.
